study_design: Pooled prospective cohort analysis of the Miyagi Cohort Study and Ohsaki Cohort Study
cohort_total_n_excerpt: In the present study, a total of 36,499 men, aged 40-79 years, who participated in the Miyagi Cohort Study in 1990 and in the Ohsaki Cohort Study in 1994 were followed for a median of 13.2 years.
reason: The abstract reports incident total prostate cancer. Although it states that the relationship did not differ by clinical stage, it does not identify or define an advanced, high-grade, or other explicitly aggressive incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Compared to participants with mushroom consumption <1 time/week, frequent mushroom intake was associated with a decreased risk of prostate cancer (1-2 times/week: HRs [95% CIs] = 0.92 [0.81, 1.05]; ≥3 times/week: HRs [95% CIs] = 0.83 [0.70, 0.98]; p-trend = 0.023).
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate is explicitly for prostate cancer incidence overall, not an aggressive subtype.
